about.title: Sausalito Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Sausalito's hillside stairways, waterfront boardwalks, and tightly packed shops along Bridgeway create plenty of spots where a wet floor, a broken step, or a loose cable can catch someone off guard. When that happens on someone else's property, figuring out who's accountable isn't always straightforward. California law asks whether the property owner or business knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That's why documenting what caused your fall matters so much, especially in a small city like Sausalito where many businesses rely on surveillance systems that may only hold footage briefly. LawProactive doesn't represent clients directly; we're a free service that connects you with an independent local attorney who can evaluate your fall, gather evidence before it disappears, and explain your options. There's no obligation and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Sausalito Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timing
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help pin down how long a spill, crack, or broken railing existed before you fell.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Doesn't Last
items.desc: Many Sausalito shops and waterfront businesses overwrite security video within days. Acting quickly to request preservation can be the difference in supporting your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a share of damages proportional to fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If a government entity owns the property, such as a public walkway or municipal building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early administrative claim. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I fell on wet pavement near the Sausalito waterfront?
items.answer: Weather-related conditions near the water can complicate a claim because owners often argue the hazard was open and obvious or caused by nature rather than neglect. What matters is whether the property owner had a reasonable chance to address the wet or uneven surface and failed to. Photos, witness names, and timing of the incident all help clarify that.

items.question: Will I still get anything if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows a pure comparative fault system, meaning your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated entirely. An independent attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your specific case.
